answer: Each identity leases one ferrous stack slot and locks a 70-credit bond, then files its plume opacity log each epoch, stamped by its pulse-timed sampler. An auditor recomputes opacity from the camera log and checks pulse-tick continuity against its register; a gap, reused tick chain, or mismatch burns the bond. The first lease costs 31, the k-th 31+6(k-1), so the 1000th costs 6025 and 1,000 fakes pay 3,028,000 plus 70,000 locked. A rented-stack ring fails: one sampler yields one tick chain per epoch, one slot per chain. An honest operator pays 31 once, reclaiming the bond after a clean audit.
